title: Formal School Instructor-Pilot/Naval Flight Officer (I) (LtCol to 2ndLt) EMOS (7509, 7518, 7523, 7532, 7543, 7557, 7525, 7588, 7562, 7563, 7564, 7565, 7566), CG TECOM
raw_text:
10. MOS 0956, Formal School Instructor-Pilot/Naval Flight Officer (I) (LtCol
to 2ndLt) EMOS (7509, 7518, 7523, 7532, 7543, 7557, 7525, 7588, 7562, 7563,
7564, 7565, 7566), CG TECOM

    a. Summary. Marine Officers assigned to a teaching billet or faculty
position, that facilitate learning as their primary duty in a designated
course approved by the appropriate general/flag officer in their chain of
command, may be granted an EMOS if they meet the prerequisites and
requirements outlined below. Augmented personnel support used as training
aids (e.g. role players, demonstrator cadre) for instruction do not meet the
criteria to be instructors.

       b.   Prerequisites

            (1) Fully qualified in the MOS aligned with the instructor billet.

        (2) Security requirement: eligible for top secret special
compartmented intelligence clearance.

       c.   Requirements

        (1) Must meet the prerequisites prescribed in MCO 1553.2D Marine
Corps Formal School Management Policy Guidance.




                                          1-64                       Enclosure (1)
 1111                                                           NAVMC 1200.1L



        (2) Completion of a TRNGCMD approved instructor course either an
approved Marine Corps or service level approved instructor service course
(other services pertain).

        (3) Demonstrated level of proficiency and successful completion of
duties while serving in an instructor billet.

        (4) Serve in a specified TRNGCMD instructor designated billet
identification code (BIC) billet for a period of not less than six months.

        (5) Approved award of the EMOS by a TRNGCMD commander or TRNGCMD
school director in the grade of O5 or above.

        (6) Commanding General, TRNGCMD will be the approving authority for
all waivers where Marines are not currently assigned to fill a designated
instructor billet BIC, time serving in the billet, and any other request
which does not meet the requirements listed above.

       d.   Duties

        (1) Collaborate with formal school staff responsible for learning
design to ensure seamless transition into course implementation.

        (2) Employ MarineNet eLearning ecosystem to enable learner self-study
with accountability.

        (3) Prepare for and facilitate learning during specific course
lessons to achieve learning objectives and associated learning outcomes that
meet service defined common or occupational learning requirements.

        (4) Cultivate and sustain open and challenging learning climates
within lessons to prompt learners to engage and collaborate.

        (5) Guide lesson activities and debriefs, exploiting learning
opportunities as they emerge, per approved lesson files, course learning
outcomes, and local faculty qualification requirements.

        (6) Lead active learner-centered methods, including chalk talks,
gallery walks, jigsaws, discussions, decision-forcing cases, decision games,
practical applications, field exercises, and wargaming opportunities among
others.

        (7) Proctor assessments and exams per the approved graders guide to
assess learning and provide learners with feedback while maintaining the
integrity of each action.

        (8) Mentor and coach students regarding their academic progress,
learning, and professional development.

        (9) Continue personal and professional development through feedback
collection, learning trends research, critical self-assessment, goal setting,
developmental course and activity completion, and confirmed performance
improvement.

        (10) Process lesson evaluation data and form recommendations to
support course review boards.




                                     1-65                        Enclosure (1)
 1111                                                               NAVMC 1200.1L



        (11) Professionally contribute to review boards and working groups
related to resource optimization in meeting defined service learning
requirements.

    e. Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code.
Teachers and Instructors, All Other 25-3099.

       f.   Related Military Skill.   None.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
